extractedText: Leadership Shakeup at Bulgari: A New Era Begins with Laura Burdese at the Helm In a move that’s sure to ripple through the luxury industry, Bulgari has announced Laura Burdese as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1. This transition marks the end of Jean-Christophe Babin’s tenure as CEO, though he’ll remain a pivotal figure as chairman of the Bulgari board, CEO of the Bulgari Hotel business unit, and president of the Bulgari Foundation. But here’s where it gets intriguing: Burdese’s appointment isn’t just a change in leadership—it’s a testament to her proven track record and a bold step into a new chapter for the iconic Roman jewelry maison. And this is the part most people miss: Burdese’s rise to the top is rooted in her diverse experience across beauty, fashion, and luxury, making her uniquely positioned to steer Bulgari’s future. A Seamless Transition—or Is It? Stéphane Bianchi, LVMH group managing director, praised the transition as ‘smooth,’ highlighting the collaborative efforts of Burdese and Babin over the past three years. But let’s pause for a moment: Can a leadership change at a luxury powerhouse ever truly be seamless? Bianchi’s confidence in Burdese’s ‘strong contribution and accomplishments’ is undeniable, yet the question remains: How will her vision differ from Babin’s? After all, Babin’s legacy includes not only Bulgari’s success but also his transformative work at TAG Heuer. Will Burdese continue his trajectory, or will she chart a new course? Controversial thought: Could this shift signal a subtle rebalancing of Bulgari’s focus between jewelry and its expanding hotel empire?See AlsoThe Best Dressed Celebrities of December 2025R13 Pre-Fall 2026 Collection: Punk Grunge Meets Classic MenswearLeonard and Georg Lux Part Ways: Fashion News UpdateRobert Wun: From Fear to Fashion | Couture Designer's Journey Burdese’s Journey: From Beauty to Luxury Dominance Burdese’s career is a masterclass in versatility. Starting in the beauty industry with roles at Beiersdorf and L’Oréal, she transitioned to the Swatch Group in 1999, eventually becoming president and CEO of Calvin Klein Watch & Jewelry. Her move to LVMH in 2016 as CEO of Acqua di Parma and later as Bulgari’s vice president of marketing and communications solidified her reputation as a strategic leader. But here’s the kicker: Her appointment as CEO comes at a time when Bulgari is not just a jewelry brand but a global lifestyle icon. How will her background in beauty and watches influence Bulgari’s future collections and brand identity? Babin’s Legacy: A Watchmaking Revolution and BeyondSee AlsoRunway’s GWM-1: Revolutionizing World Models Beyond Hollywood - AI, Robotics, and Beyond! Under Babin’s leadership, Bulgari’s watchmaking segment soared to new heights, culminating in the 2024 WWD Honor for Watch Brand of the Year for the Octo Finissimo Ultra COSC—the world’s thinnest mechanical watch. Yet, his impact extends beyond timepieces. Babin’s expansion of Bulgari’s luxury hotels to nine locations, including Rome, Paris, and Tokyo, has cemented the brand’s presence in the hospitality sector. But here’s the controversial question: With Babin now overseeing LVMH Watches, including Hublot and Zenith, will Bulgari’s watch division maintain its momentum, or will it take a backseat to other LVMH brands? Bulgari’s Bold Moves: From Valenza to Venice One of Burdese’s first challenges will be building on the success of Bulgari’s new production facility in Valenza, Italy, inaugurated in April. Touted as the largest single-brand jewelry manufacturing site globally, the facility also houses the Scuola Bulgari, a publicly accessible training school. This move underscores Bulgari’s commitment to craftsmanship and education—a point of pride for Babin, who emphasized that Bulgari is the only jeweler producing its pieces entirely in its country of origin. But here’s where it gets controversial: In an era of globalization, is this localization strategy sustainable, or is it a niche play that could limit scalability? Experiential Luxury: Bulgari’s 140th Anniversary and Beyond Bulgari hasn’t just been crafting jewelry; it’s been crafting experiences. From Venice to Taormina, the brand has hosted high-profile events featuring ambassadors like Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, and Blackpink’s Lisa. These experiential campaigns have elevated Bulgari’s visibility, but at what cost? Thought-provoking question: As luxury brands increasingly blur the lines between product and experience, is Bulgari risking its heritage by leaning too heavily into celebrity-driven events? The Future of Bulgari: A Conversation Starter As Burdese steps into her new role, the luxury world watches with bated breath. Will she maintain Bulgari’s focus on Italian craftsmanship, or will she pivot toward global trends? How will she balance the brand’s jewelry and hospitality ventures?
